title: [Project] Web Design Agency Website
summary: Section 8 capstone: take a plain starter page for a design agency and use float, display, inline/block behaviour and a media query to produce a two-card layout that stacks on phones. The walkthrough afterwards highlights three details: a span for partial colouring, the 680px breakpoint, and object-fit.

concepts.heading: What the finished page looks like
points: Header area with a logo, then an h1 along the lines of 'We are a Creative Design Agency', then two side-by-side cards (image + title + paragraph each), then a footer with the company motto.
On wide screens the left card floats left and the right card floats right, each about 45% wide, so they form two columns.
On narrow screens (roughly phone width) the cards stop being columns and stack vertically, each spanning the full width, with centred heading and justified text.

concepts.heading: Skills the project is meant to exercise
points: Block vs inline vs inline-block behaviour (the display property).
float: left / float: right (and clear for the footer) to build columns and wrap text around images.
Responsiveness through a viewport meta tag and a max-width media query.
The brief explicitly says an identical copy is not required: any attractive layout that uses these tools is acceptable; breaking the problem down yourself is the real goal.

concepts.heading: Working with the starter files
points: Starter folder contains index.html (the file to edit, already has fonts, images and text but no layout), solution.html and its stylesheet, plus an assets/images folder (logo, two card images).
Open both index.html and solution.html in Live Preview side by side; copy the preview URL into a real browser to resize the window and test the breakpoint.
Recommended order: attempt it yourself first, only then read the solution. Share especially good variations in the course Q&A.

concepts.heading: Solution walkthrough: key details
points: The word 'Creative' is wrapped in <span class="creative"> so only that word gets its own colour (midnightblue) while staying in the normal text flow; span is an inline element so it does not break the line.
Cards use two layout classes plus a shared class: class="left card" and class="right card". .card sets width: 45%; .left floats left; .right floats right.
Card images use a .tile-image class with a fixed height (200px), float: left and a right margin, so the title and paragraph wrap around the image.

A media query for max-width: 680px targets phones and small tablets. Inside it: .card gets display: block, width: 100%, a bottom margin and text-align: justify; the card image gets width: 100%, display: inline and object-fit: cover; the h1 shrinks and is centred; the logo is made smaller.
text-align: justify stretches each line to both edges so the paragraph looks like a clean block on a narrow screen.

object-fit is new in this lesson: it controls how an image fills a box whose size differs from the image's aspect ratio (cover crops to fill without distortion). Advice given: when you meet an unfamiliar property, look it up on MDN; that is normal professional workflow.

(Extra) The reference CSS also makes body a flex column with min-height: 95vh and gives .main flex: 1 so the footer sticks to the bottom of short pages; that is a flexbox trick from the next section and is not explained here.

(Extra) The starter footer needs to sit below the floated cards; in the reference this works because .main is a flex item that contains the floats, otherwise clear: both on the footer is the classic fix.

task.name: Section 8 project: Web Design Agency Website
task.starting_point: Starter index.html with fonts, logo, two card images, headings, paragraphs and a footer already in place, but with no layout CSS; a solution.html is included for comparison.
task.goal: Style the page into a two-column card layout using float/display and make it responsive so the cards stack on narrow screens.
steps: Open index.html and solution.html in Live Preview and compare; open the preview URL in a full browser so the window can be resized.
Wrap the word 'Creative' in a span with a class and colour it in the stylesheet.
Give both cards a width (about 45%), float one left and one right so they sit side by side.
Float the card images left with a right margin so the text wraps around them.
Add a max-width media query (around 600-680px) that gives the cards full width and display: block so they stack, and adjust image, heading and text alignment for small screens.
Resize the browser to check the breakpoint, then compare with solution.html and look up unfamiliar properties such as object-fit on MDN.
task.expected_result: Wide screen: two floated cards side by side below the heading, footer at the bottom. Narrow screen: cards stacked full width with justified text and a centred heading.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 08 - Advanced CSS/08.05 - Web Design Agency Project/solution.css

pitfalls: Floated cards collapse their parent's height, so the footer can ride up unless the parent contains the floats or the footer uses clear: both.
Forgetting the viewport meta tag, which stops media queries behaving as expected on phones.
Peeking at the solution before attempting the layout.
The reference repo's solution.html has an author footer ('Made with love by ...') that is not part of the course.

playground.coverage: Covers the span for 'Creative', floating the two cards, floating the images so text wraps, and clearing the footer. Uses a 120px image and 45% cards, with a media query only suggested as a go-further bullet.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a task for the max-width media query that stacks the cards (display: block; width: 100%) since responsiveness is a core part of the real project.
Add a task introducing object-fit: cover on the images in the stacked layout, with a demo toggling fill/contain/cover.
Add text-align: justify and centred h1 for the mobile view as a small styling step.
Add a viewport-width slider in the explore demo to show the breakpoint flip at 680px.
Mention that the project is open-ended (alternative designs welcome).
